sections.heading: Sharing contract and qualification
sections.markdown: The settled target contract requires Sendable arguments and captures at go boundaries and forbids every ordinary outer var capture, including reads. Const, COW, and atomic reference counts alone do not prove Sendable. These are language contracts, not evidence that the complete go, Task, resource, or synchronization families are implemented in new XIR; qualification follows spec §17.

sections.heading: Owned Task errors
sections.markdown: Task terminal errors use the actual worker entry's certificate in the same Program. Complete bounded graph admission precedes exact enum type/variant membership; the same runtime Domain prepays the immutable Effects scan bound without debiting compiler resources. Current payload families include Array, Nullable, Tuple, enum, struct, explicit Sendable class, Atomic and Task fields, including direct Tasks and Arrays of Tasks. Repeated owned copies survive Instance and final code-lease retirement without consuming the sticky result. Compiler Sendable proof still covers every Error variant. Full parameter, generator, scheduler and product safety qualification remain separate (spec 10.12/17).

sections.heading: Closed Task argument carriers
sections.markdown: Task arguments use the same closed copyable scalar, Array, Nullable, Tuple, enum, struct, explicit Sendable class, Atomic and Task carriers as executable results, with Unit excluded from the ordinary argument domain. Complete Checked Sendable and worker root-effect proof remain mandatory. Call prepares owned graphs before child publication; later parent Array mutation preserves the child's logical copy, while Atomic and Task retain identity. Inheritance, full argument fault injection and product safety remain separately qualified (spec 10.12/17).

sections.heading: Explicit Sendable class carriers
sections.markdown: An explicit implements Sendable class records the intrinsic marker in sole nominal metadata. Every field proves Sendable in the authentic declaration environment and is readonly after construction; ordinary classes and same-name interfaces cannot infer or forge the promise. Task arguments, results and Error fields retain class identity; Atomic fields keep synchronized identity and extracted Array fields remain value copies. Checked decode and Lowered identity tables reject marker-plus-mutable-field contradictions. The development slice covers root classes and bounded generics, including real finite recursive class chains. Bounded proof closes a cycle only through a verified readonly class identity edge and checks every sibling; value-only cycles and outer-class laundering reject. Inheritance and full fault-injection/product safety qualification remain separate (spec 10.12/17).

sections.heading: Value arguments and declared consumption
sections.markdown: Copyable, Sendable values pass as logical copies; ordinary Array arguments do not require copy(array), explicit move, or unique backing. Copying stops at class and synchronization identities. Only noncopyable resources use consuming parameter declarations; an explicit move marker may identify that transfer. Complete go admission remains a separate obligation.

sections.heading: Atomic — lock-free shared state
sections.markdown:
`Atomic<T>` wraps `i64`, `f64`, or `bool` with C11 atomic operations. Name it with `const`; its audited methods provide synchronized interior mutation.

Methods: `load`, `store`, `add`, `sub`, `fetchAdd`, `fetchSub`, `swap`, `compareExchange`, `toggle`, `toString`.

All methods accept optional `Ordering` enum (default `SeqCst`): `Relaxed`, `Acquire`, `Release`, `AcquireRelease`, `SeqCst`.

```xray
const counter = Atomic(0)
counter.add(1)
var (old, ok) = counter.compareExchange(1, 42)
print(counter.load())  // 42
```

Frozen next cutover: Ordering identity and permissions are rechecked; compareExchange returns a real owned Tuple prepared before cell access. f64 transport preserves every binary64 payload, while numeric results stay canonical. One f64 CAS attempt per resume continues on failure without suspension or a second pipeline. Complete execution and unsupported-target admission remain pending implementation and qualification (spec 10.9/17.24).

sections.heading: Locks — explicit execution domain
sections.markdown:
`sync.*` locks are coroutine-domain primitives: they may suspend and require `import sync`. `sys.Os*` locks are OS-thread-domain primitives: they block the current OS thread and require `import sys`. Name synchronization handles with `const`; their audited methods provide synchronized interior mutation.

```xray
import sync
import sys

const m = sync.Mutex<i64>(0)
const os_m = sys.OsMutex()
```
